synthesis: DEV-2059 asks for a disposition control in the Scout hit modal, a Scout API endpoint to persist it, and a markers-query filter so bad hits fall off the map/counts. Verifying every 'leverage this infra' claim against current main shows the ticket is significantly stale: the disposition write pipeline (Scan::updateDisposition -> Postgres write -> SyncDispositionToClickhouse dispatch -> 5-table CH ALTER UPDATE) is fully wired and already dispatched (restored by DEV-2176 on 2026-07-09, after an earlier commit 1b241ae1 had removed it -- the ticket's 'never dispatched' claim is a snapshot of that intermediate, since-fixed state). More importantly, the canonical disposition ALLOWLIST (forDispositions([NEW_HIT, VALID]) via App\Clickhouse\Models\Hit::scopeValidDisposition/scopeLiveValid) is ALREADY applied to every Scout read surface: both map-marker endpoints (ClarityScoutMapController::hits driver, ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::hits admin), both stats endpoints, both recentHits endpoints, and the hit-density heatmap (HitDirectHotspotQuery). All of this is pinned by existing tests (test_map_hits_excludes_rejected_dispositions, test_recent_hits_filters_by_disposition, test_stats_excludes_hits_with_rejected_dispositions). So the 'add forDispositions to the markers query' scope item is DONE already (via DEV-2113/DEV-2117), and once a hit's disposition changes to anything outside {null, Valid}, it will already fall off the map/counts automatically -- provided the CH sync completes. What genuinely remains, confirmed missing by direct inspection: (1) the Scout hit modal (resources/js/clarity-scout/components/MapShell.vue, built by DEV-2058) has zero disposition UI; (2) there is no Sanctum-authenticated Scout API route to call Scan::updateDisposition() -- the only existing disposition route (POST /scan/disposition, DispositionController) sits behind session ('auth') middleware and is called via axios/cookies (resources/js/app.js:94-128), which the Scout PWA's bearer-token client (resources/js/clarity-scout/lib/fetch.js) cannot use, and the admin Bird's-Eye surface uses a THIRD auth mode (web session + CSRF, no Sanctum) via a completely separate route prefix; (3) none of the hit payloads the modal actually renders (map hits() -- no id field at all; recentHits() -- carries id, but that is the ClickHouse Hit's own id, NOT scan_id, per the confirmed hits_cold/hits_hot schema where id and scan_id are distinct columns) carry the scan_id the disposition write needs, so a scan_id field must be added to those payloads before the modal can submit anything. The real remaining work is materially smaller than the ticket implies, but has real open design questions (admin vs. driver scope, endpoint tenancy, and how soon a change should visually take effect given the PG-write -> queued-job -> async-CH-mutation -> poll-cache chain).

notes: Ticket premise 'SyncDispositionToClickhouse job EXISTS but is NEVER dispatched' is FALSE on current main. It was true only transiently: commit 1b241ae1 (Apr 14) removed the dispatch to rely on Postgres-only reads; DEV-2176 (2026-07-09) restored it after that approach was found too slow (see docs/investigations/DEV-2176/journal.md line 18: ~3.7s/query on the 3.5B-row hits_cold table). Scan::updateDisposition() now writes Postgres synchronously then calls the private syncDispositionToClickhouse() helper, which dispatches the job (app/Models/Scan.php:513-591).

Ticket premise 'the map markers query does NOT yet' filter by disposition is FALSE on current main. Both ClarityScoutMapController::hits() (driver) and ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::hits() (admin) already call ->validDisposition() (lines 216 and 305 respectively), added as part of DEV-2113/DEV-2117 (App\Clickhouse\Models\Hit.php git-blamed 2026-06-30, predating this ticket). This is pinned by tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutMapControllerTest.php:615 (test_map_hits_excludes_rejected_dispositions).
DispositionEnum, Scan::updateDisposition(), and BulkDispositionAction all VERIFIED TRUE exactly as the ticket describes -- no drift.

The canonical disposition rule (App\Clickhouse\Models\Hit::scopeValidDisposition, DEV-2080) is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist: a hit stays visible only when disposition IS NULL (i.e. unset/NEW_HIT) or 'Valid'; every other DispositionEnum case (Accessible, Moving, Inaccessible, Invalid Scan, Invalid, Reviewed) already hides it everywhere this scope is used. This answers the ticket's own open question about 'exactly which cases should hide a marker' -- the answer is already implemented and uniform across every current Scout surface.

The existing DispositionPopup Blade/Alpine component (resources/views/components/scans/disposition-popup.blade.php) plus resources/js/app.js:94-128 is a closer UI precedent than BulkDispositionAction for a Vue equivalent: a <select> of DispositionEnum::formOptions(), gated reason-capture grid shown only for 'Invalid Scan', and axios POST to /scan/disposition with {scan_id, disposition, reason}.

That existing /scan/disposition route cannot be reused as-is by the Scout PWA: it sits behind web 'auth' session middleware (routes/web.php:88) and is called via axios+cookies, whereas the Scout driver client (resources/js/clarity-scout/lib/fetch.js) authenticates with a Bearer token from localStorage, and the admin Bird's-Eye client uses a third pattern (web session + CSRF header under a completely different route prefix, /scout/org-map/api). A genuinely new endpoint is required for the driver path at minimum.

grounding.code_flow: Write path (existing, works today): DispositionController@__invoke (or any future Scout controller) -> Scan::updateDisposition() [app/Models/Scan.php:513] -> updateOrCreateMetadata()->updateQuietly() writes Postgres scans_metadata.meta->disposition synchronously -> private syncDispositionToClickhouse() -> SyncDispositionToClickhouse::dispatch() queues the job on `{low}` -> job handle() runs 5 ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE statements against clarity_clickhouse_write (async CH mutation) -> once applied, the flat `disposition` column on hits_cold/hits_hot/scans_cold/scans_hot/missed_opportunities reflects the new value. Read path (existing, already filtered): any Scout surface builds its query on App\Clickhouse\Models\Hit (or the raw HitDirectHotspotQuery SQL) and calls ->validDisposition()/->liveValid(), which resolves to WHERE disposition IS NULL OR disposition IN (...) against that same flat column -- so once the mutation lands, the hit silently drops out of every poll. The ticket's remaining gap sits entirely BEFORE this chain: there is no UI to trigger it and no reachable endpoint from the Scout client to call updateDisposition() in the first place.

data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: The flat `disposition` column on the 5 CH tables is NOT CDC-replicated from Postgres -- it is written exclusively by the app-level SyncDispositionToClickhouse job's ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE mutations, dispatched from Scan::updateDisposition(). DEV-2176 explicitly tried and reverted repointing Scout's disposition READS onto the live CDC/scans_metadata source (measured ~3.7s/query on hits_cold at 3.5B rows) -- any DEV-2059 implementation must keep reading the flat column via forDispositions()/validDisposition(), not join/subquery against scans_metadata. ClickHouse ALTER UPDATE mutations are asynchronous server-side even after the statement returns, so there is an unbounded (if normally short) window between the job completing and the row actually reflecting the new disposition in a SELECT.
data_impact.indexes_relied_on: hits_cold/hits_hot: INDEX idx_disposition-equivalent is NOT present on hits tables (only scans_cold/scans_hot declare `INDEX idx_disposition disposition TYPE set(20)`); hits_cold/hits_hot disposition filtering rides on the existing ORDER BY (hotlist_org_id, toYYYYMM(...), ..., id) plus the other selective WHERE clauses (hotlist_org_id/kit_org_id, hit_type, hit_created_at range) already present in every query before ->validDisposition() is applied -- worth flagging as a perf watch-item given DEV-2176's cost lesson, though this is a cheap flat-column predicate, not a join, so it should be far cheaper than the reverted CDC-repoint approach.

escalate.reason: Confidence in the CODE FACTS is high (every claim above is file:line-grounded and several directly contradict the ticket's stated premises, which is itself useful signal to surface). The escalation is recommended because of the open DESIGN questions a human should resolve before implementation, not because the code investigation is shaky: (1) whether the disposition control ships driver-only or also to admin Bird's-Eye -- this roughly doubles backend surface area given the two auth transports; (2) the endpoint's tenancy scope (kit vs org); (3) the acceptable UX latency given the multi-stage async chain (queue + CH mutation + poll TTL), where the existing admin-popup precedent optimistically removes the row client-side rather than waiting. None of these are answerable from the codebase alone, and getting them wrong risks either an under-scoped PR (missing admin support if that's expected) or a needlessly large one (building the admin path if it's not wanted) -- exactly the kind of complexity blow-up the ticket itself already flags as a risk for deprioritization.
